input: This executive summary reviews delivery performance across the firm, which operates 2 plants and generates revenue of $99 million per year. The evidence base consists of order records for 12 months, encompassing a total of 16050 orders. Over the last two quarters, on-time delivery stood at 91%, against a target of 95%, while overtime cost reached $2 million last year, an increase of 19% on the year before. The order backlog currently stands at 3.6 weeks, compared with 1.6 weeks a year ago, meaning that the backlog has more than doubled even as delivery performance has remained stubbornly below target. A closer examination of the figures reveals that Plant 2 accounts for some 55% of all late orders, highlighting the extent to which the problem is concentrated at a single site. A scheduling system covering all plants has been quoted at $329k, with Plant 2 alone quoted at $132k, and an internal estimate suggests that the overtime reduction at Plant 2 could be in the region of 15–20% in the first year, although it should be noted that this is an internal estimate rather than a vendor figure. The recommendation under consideration is therefore to install the system at Plant 2 in the first instance, committing $132k, and to hold the remaining plant until Plant 2 results have been reported and evaluated, so that the Plant 2 outcome determines whether the wider rollout proceeds, with the operations director owning the scheduling programme throughout.

Delivery performance and cost have moved together throughout: the operation that ships late is the operation that buys the overtime, and both stand in the same plant's record. The hold on the remaining plant is reversible at the point the first result is reported. The second plant follows only on that evidence, and not before.
